questions.question: Method discountTotal() reads four fields off the Order object and touches none of its own class's data; reviewers say it belongs inside Order. Which smell is this?
questions.explanation: Feature Envy = a method that envies another class's data; the remedy is usually Move Method into the envied class.

questions.question: A pricing routine switches on birdType (EUROPEAN, AFRICAN, NORWEGIAN_BLUE); every new type forces edits to the same growing conditional. Which refactoring pushes each branch into an overridden method on a per-type subclass?
questions.explanation: Moving each branch into a subclass's overridden method removes the switch entirely and makes new types an extension, not an edit.

questions.question: Every public method of OrderFacade merely forwards its call unchanged to OrderService, adding no logic of its own. Which smell names such a delegating class?
questions.explanation: A Middle Man only delegates; the fix is Remove Middle Man so clients talk to the class that actually does the work.

questions.question: A developer burns a sprint building a generic plugin framework for integrations no customer has requested, 'just in case' it is needed later. Which XP principle says this work should not have been done?
alternatives: You Aren't Going to Need It
questions.explanation: YAGNI forbids speculative functionality: implement it when it is actually needed, not in anticipation.

questions.question: Class SecurityUtil is depended upon by 12 other classes, while it itself depends on 2 external classes. Which coupling metric does the number 12 represent?
questions.explanation: Afferent coupling (Ca, fan-in) counts incoming dependencies - how many classes rely on this one; the 2 outgoing deps are its Ce.

questions.question: class Money has only private fields plus public getters and setters; every piece of currency logic lives in a separate PricingUtils class. Which smell does the anemic Money class exhibit?
questions.explanation: A Data Class holds fields but no behavior; encapsulation is broken because the operations belong inside the class that owns the data.

questions.question: Code review finds `if (orderTotal > 30)` repeated in seven files, where 30 silently means the free-shipping threshold. Which refactoring turns the literal into a named constant?
questions.answer: Replace Magic Number with Symbolic Constant
questions.explanation: Replacing the magic literal with a named constant makes intent explicit and gives a single point of change.

questions.question: Class ReportEngine has Ca = 3 (incoming dependents) and Ce = 7 (outgoing dependencies). Compute its instability I = Ce / (Ca + Ce).
questions.explanation: I = Ce / (Ca + Ce) = 7 / (3 + 7) = 0.7; values near 1 mean a class is volatile, near 0 mean stable.

questions.question: class Stack extends Vector, but callers must never touch the parent's elementAt() or insertElementAt(); the subclass effectively refuses half the API it inherited. Which smell is this?
questions.explanation: Refused Bequest signals the subclass rejects its inheritance - the hierarchy is wrong; delegation would fit better.

questions.question: Two methods share identical cyclomatic complexity, yet the one that nests its conditions four levels deep with early returns is far harder for humans to follow. Which metric - unlike cyclomatic complexity - penalizes that nesting?
questions.explanation: Cognitive Complexity adds increments for nesting and flow breaks, so it tracks human understandability rather than raw path count.

questions.question: Clients write a.getAddress().getCity(). To reduce this coupling, you add a method on 'a' that forwards the call. Which refactoring is this?
questions.explanation: Hide Delegate creates a method on the server object that delegates the call, removing the client's dependency on the chain.

questions.question: Module Checkout imports 9 external classes and is itself imported by 4 other classes. Give its efferent coupling and its instability, I = Ce / (Ca + Ce).
questions.explanation: Efferent coupling counts outgoing dependencies: the 9 imported classes, so Ce = 9 while Ca = 4 (the importers). Instability I = Ce / (Ca + Ce) = 9 / 13 ~ 0.69, fairly volatile.

questions.question: Class D inherits from C, which inherits from B, which inherits from root class A. In the Chidamber-Kemerer suite, what is D's Depth of Inheritance Tree value?
questions.explanation: DIT counts the hops from the class to the hierarchy root: D -> C -> B -> A is 3 levels deep.

questions.question: A method contains a huge switch statement dispatching on a 'type' field. Which code smell is this?
questions.explanation: The Switch Statements smell scatters type-based branching; Replace Conditional with Polymorphism is the classic fix.

questions.question: Dozens of functions across the system all read and write one shared global variable. Which coupling type is this?
questions.explanation: Common (global) coupling arises when modules share global data, making changes ripple unpredictably across the system.

questions.question: Compute the cyclomatic complexity of a method containing 3 if-statements, 1 for-loop, and a switch with 4 cases (each case counts as one decision).
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity M = decision points + 1 = (3 ifs + 1 loop + 4 cases) + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9.

questions.question: A function takes a boolean 'flag' that selects between two completely different behaviors (export-to-PDF vs send-email). Name the smell, and the refactoring that splits it into two explicit methods.
questions.answer: Control flag (flag argument); fixed with Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods
alternatives: Flag argument - Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods
questions.explanation: A boolean that switches behavior is a control flag; Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods creates one clearly named method per behavior.

questions.question: Class Order exposes 4 methods, and those methods invoke 7 distinct methods on other classes. In the Chidamber-Kemerer suite, what is Order's Response for a Class value?
questions.explanation: RFC = local methods + methods they call = 4 + 7 = 11; a high RFC means one message can trigger a large, hard-to-test call tree.

questions.question: A shared utility introduced to remove duplication is stateful and only works correctly when its methods are called in a specific order, so all callers now silently depend on call sequence. Which type of coupling does this introduce?
questions.explanation: Temporal coupling exists when components must be invoked in a particular order or at a particular time; it is hidden and fragile.

questions.question: A team splits a 3,000-line God class into Customer, Order, and Billing classes. Beyond removing the Large Class smell, which internal design quality does each new class gain?
questions.explanation: Each resulting class groups only elements serving a single responsibility, raising cohesion while lowering coupling between classes.
